title: differential growth · 3D upward tower
concept: 7ea was effectively 2D — curve on the XZ plane with a tiny age-based Y sink. 5gm is the 3D answer: the curve evolves in full 3D space and each vertex experiences a slow upward drift proportional to its own age. Newly-subdivided midpoints inherit young age and stay near the base; older vertices rise. The result is a coral tower that grows UP over time — a vertical record of evolution rather than a horizontal sprawl. Camera follows the rising target. Color is height-graded: bright algae at the base (young, just-grown) → coral red at mid → bone/silver at top (oldest, risen highest).
notes: Direct response to user feedback: 'create a new one like 7ea but it has 3d movement along z (upward axis)'. Replaces uxh in the favorites pool. Pre-warms 800 steps so the tower opens with established structure. 3D spatial hash for repulsion (cell key includes y dimension). Vertical pressure is dampened (0.4x of horizontal) so the form ribbons up rather than ballooning. Cap at 4000 vertices.
